# Moving panes and tabs (after Rex): out of a split into a tab of its own,
# into another tab's split, into a window of their own, and a window's tab
# into another window. Programs keep running through every move: the sleep
# keeps going, and what the program prints after a move shows where it went.
type:echo LEFT-PANE
key:enter
wait:0.8
key:cmd+d
wait:1.2
type:echo RIGHT-PANE; sleep 5.@N@; echo LATE-OUTPUT; sleep 299.@N@
key:enter
wait:0.8
expect-tab:2 panes
# Out of the split into a tab of its own, after this one.
action:move_surface_to_new_tab
expect-tab-count:2
expect-shell:echo n=$(pgrep -f 'sleep 299[.]@N@' | wc -l | tr -d ' ') ==> n=0
expect-shell:echo n=$(pgrep -f 'sleep 5[.]@N@' | wc -l | tr -d ' ') ==> n=1
# Back: alone in its tab, it joins tab 1 and its tab goes.
action:move_surface_to_tab:1
expect-tab-count:1
expect-tab:2 panes
# Into a window of its own; the split here is one pane again. What it
# prints from now on shows there.
action:move_surface_to_new_window
expect-windows:2
expect-tab-count:1
expect:LEFT-PANE
wait:4.0
expect-other:LATE-OUTPUT
expect-not:LATE-OUTPUT
expect-shell:echo n=$(pgrep -f 'sleep 299[.]@N@' | wc -l | tr -d ' ') ==> n=1
# A window's only tab can't leave it for a new one (there'd be nothing left).
action:move_tab_to_new_window
expect-windows:2
# The other window's only tab comes back here; that window closes, the program runs on.
take-tab:1
wait:0.5
expect-windows:1
expect-tab-count:2
expect:LATE-OUTPUT
expect-shell:echo n=$(pgrep -f 'sleep 299[.]@N@' | wc -l | tr -d ' ') ==> n=1
# With two tabs, the one in front can go to a window of its own.
action:move_tab_to_new_window
expect-windows:2
expect-tab-count:1
expect-other:LATE-OUTPUT
# A move asked for twice in a row moves the pane once; so does a park right before it.
key:cmd+d
wait:1.2
key:cmd+d
wait:1.2
action:move_surface_to_new_tab,move_surface_to_new_tab
expect-tab-count:2
action:goto_tab:1
action:park_surface,move_surface_to_new_tab
expect-tab-count:2
expect-tab:1 parked
